data.name: The Bahamas
data.summary: The Bahamas levies no personal income tax, capital gains tax, dividend tax, inheritance, estate, gift or net wealth tax. The costs that do apply are on Bahamian real estate: VAT of up to 10% on conveyances (10% flat for foreign buyers), annual real property tax, and probate/resealing formalities for Bahamian-situs assets. No income tax treaties. Economic permanent residence needs a USD 1 million investment (real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds) held 10 years, up from USD 750,000 since 1 January 2025.

regimes.name: Ordinary residence
regimes.description: No direct taxes on individuals; residence has no income-tax consequence.
regimes.eligibility: Any lawful resident. Non-Bahamians need a residence permit (annual, homeowner or permanent residence).

capital_gains.summary: No capital gains tax. Gains on shares, bonds, private companies and real estate are not taxed.
capital_gains.important_exceptions: Real estate conveyances bear VAT (replacing the old stamp duty on conveyances): 10% for foreign buyers and entities on the whole value; Bahamians and permanent residents with the right to work pay a sliding scale from 2.5% (under BSD 100,000) to 10% (over BSD 1 million). Base is the higher of price and fair market value; buyer and seller customarily split it 50/50 but that is a commercial choice. Transfers of shares in land-owning companies also attract VAT. Since 1 July 2025 amendments to the Conveyancing and Law of Property Act require the conveyance to be registered (anti-VAT-evasion).

A new flat 0.625% 'foreign owner-occupied' category was proposed in the 2026-27 Budget; enactment not verified.

inheritance.summary: No inheritance, estate or gift tax. A Bahamian grant of probate (or resealing of a foreign grant) is needed only for Bahamian-situs assets.
inheritance.important_exceptions: Probate/resealing: legal fees scale with Bahamian assets (minimum BSD 2,500 per Higgs & Johnson, 2012). other_transfer_cost_rate set to 0 because a portfolio held outside The Bahamas needs no Bahamian grant; Bahamian real estate passing on death may carry costs not quantified here.

open_questions: Whether stamp duty or VAT applies when Bahamian real estate vests in heirs on death (assent/vesting deed) and the size of probate fees. PwC (reviewed 21 July 2026) says only that stamp duty is levied on instruments of all types, at rates that vary, and that there are no transfer taxes; it does not address transfers on death. other_transfer_cost_rate is kept at 0 pending a primary source (Stamp Act schedule).
inheritance.gift_tax: No gift tax. Stamp duty applies to some instruments (e.g. share transfers); land transfers fall under VAT, with zero-rating for certain voluntary intra-family transfers (Chambers 2026).
inheritance.domicile_rules: No tax, so domicile and residence are irrelevant for transfer taxes. The deceased's home-country rules (e.g. US estate tax) still apply.

residency.tax_residency_test: No personal income tax, so there is no tax residence test with tax consequences.

routes.name: Economic permanent residence
routes.requirements: Minimum USD/BSD 1.0 million investment in Bahamian real estate or Central Bank of The Bahamas zero-coupon bonds, held at least 10 years (Department of Immigration). Raised from USD 750,000 with effect from 1 January 2025 (2024-25 Budget). Non-refundable processing fee BSD 200; certificate fees not verified.

routes.requirements: Available to retirees, homeowners and persons of means; conditions and fees not researched.

corporate.summary: No corporate income tax. Domestic Minimum Top-up Tax Act enacted 29 November 2024 (effective for fiscal years from 1 January 2024; for most groups from 2025) applies a 15% Pillar Two top-up only to MNE groups with revenue of EUR 750 million or more. Business licence tax applies to businesses operating locally. No withholding taxes.

income.name: The Bahamas

income_tax.summary: There is no personal income tax in The Bahamas. National Insurance is 4.65% of wages for employees and 10.3% for the self-employed, up to a weekly ceiling of BSD 830 (BSD 43,160 a year).
income_tax.self_employed_notes: Self-employed pay 10.3% of average insurable income to the National Insurance Board (NIB). Self-employed people trading locally may also owe the turnover-based annual business licence fee (Deloitte); not modelled. Cap shown is the PwC weekly ceiling BSD 830 x 52.
income_tax.local_tax_note: No income tax, no local income surtax. No health levy appears on the PwC or Deloitte pages.

regimes.name: Bahamas Extended Access Travel Stay (BEATS)
regimes.description: Annual residence permit for professionals working remotely for a non-Bahamian employer or on their own account, and for students studying remotely. The Bahamas has no personal income tax, so the permit changes access, not tax.
regimes.duration_note: Permit valid 12 months; annual renewals are considered for a maximum of three years. Fee USD 25 application + USD 1,000 permit for an individual; family adds USD 25 + USD 500 per dependant (renewal fees not listed).

Coldwell Banker Bahamas lists only luxury homes (USD 15,000 to 55,000); Bahamas Realty returned HTTP 403; the Bahamas Real Estate Association site lists vacation rentals only; Numbeo returned HTTP 429 on two attempts and Expatistan HTTP 403.

income.residence_routes: Remote workers of any citizenship (EU, US, other) can use BEATS: a 12-month permit renewable annually for up to three years, USD 1,025 for an individual. Employees of a Bahamian employer need a work permit (not researched). Permanent residence is by economic investment of BSD 1 million or more (Department of Immigration, per repo research in data/jurisdictions/BHS.json); that route is not tied to income. US citizens remain taxable in the US on worldwide income; the Bahamas has no tax to credit.
open_questions: No rent data; Nassau long-term 1-bed/2-bed rents need a listing source that can be opened (several agent sites block automated access).

immigration.name: The Bahamas
immigration.summary: The Bahamas offers permanent residence for BSD 1 million (equal to USD 1 million) in real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds held at least 10 years, up from USD 750,000 before 2025. The government processing fee is BSD 200. There is no personal income tax. EU, US and other passports use the same route.
immigration.naturalisation: Ten years as a legal permanent resident, including the 12 months before applying, and at least 6 years of residence before that final year; discretionary.
immigration.dual_citizenship_note: Sources conflict; adults reportedly must renounce other nationalities, and the factbook lists dual citizenship as not recognised. No statute was read.

routes.name: Permanent residence by investment (economic)
routes.summary: Permanent residence for BSD 1,000,000 (on a 1:1 peg with the US dollar) in Bahamian real estate or Central Bank zero-coupon bonds held for at least 10 years.
routes.requirements: Minimum investment of $1.0 million in real estate or zero-coupon bonds of the Central Bank of The Bahamas (or a mix), held at least 10 years; raised from USD 750,000 by the 2024-25 budget (effective 1 January 2025). Form IV (Permanent Residence Economic); medical certificate within 30 days; police certificate; two references; letter to the Director of Immigration.
routes.fees_note: BSD 200 non-refundable processing fee per the Department. A certificate fee of BSD 25,000 appears in one secondary guide and is not included.
routes.physical_presence: Not stated in the sources reviewed
routes.tax_note: The Bahamas has no personal income tax.
